prompt:
Implement `count_inversions(nums)` in `inversions.py`. An inversion is a pair of positions i < j where `nums[i] > nums[j]`; the function returns how many such pairs exist.

- `nums` is a list of numbers (ints or floats), which may include negatives and duplicates. Equal values are never an inversion.
- Do not mutate the input list.
- An empty list or a single-element list has 0 inversions.
- Raise `TypeError` if `nums` is not a `list`.
- This is used on large datasets, so it must stay fast: it needs to handle lists with up to 200,000 elements quickly. Comparing every pair of elements (an O(n²) approach) will be too slow - aim for an O(n log n) approach.
